pages.title: Send animation
pages.content:
Welcome to the Divoom API

    
##### command description

- send animation to device, and device will loop animation。 
This method only accepts one picture of animation at a time, and the picture format must be based on Base64 encoded RGB data.
If the animation is composed of N pictures, it will be sent in N times, one picture data will be sent each time with the picture offset。

##### Request URL
- Hardware version 90,92 is used "http://IP:80/post"
- Hardware version 96 is used "http://IP:9000/divoom_api"
  
##### Request method
- POST 

##### para

|Name|DATA TYPE|DESCRIPTION|
|:----    |:----- |-----   |
|Command |string |Draw/SendHttpGif  |
|PicNum |number |   the include single pictures of the animation and smaller than 60 |
|PicWidth |number |   the pixels of the animation, and only support the 16,32,64  |
|PicOffset |number |  the picture offset start from 0. eg:0,1,2,3,4,PicNum-1  |
|PicID |number |  the animation ID, every animation must have unique ID and auto increase,It's getting bigger and start with 1, example: the current gif id is 100, and then next gif's id should be greater than or equal to 101|
|PicSpeed |number |  the animation speed, it bases on ms |
|PicData |string |  the picutre Base64 encoded RGB data, The RGB data is  left to right and up to down |


##### request example 
we will send the gif with two frames, we will send two times,the below are two packets, the  "PicOffset=0" packet should be sended first， and the "PicOffset=1" should be sended later.
``` 
 the first packet:
 {
 "Command":"Draw/SendHttpGif",
 "PicNum":2,
 "PicWidth":64,
 "PicOffset":0,
 "PicID":3,
 "PicSpeed":100,
 "PicData":""
}

the second packet
{
 "Command":"Draw/SendHttpGif",
 "PicNum":2,
 "PicWidth":64,
 "PicOffset":1,
 "PicID":3,
 "PicSpeed":100,
 "PicData":""
}
```
##### respone example 

``` 
  {
    "error_code": 0
  }
```

##### Return value 

|Name|DATA TYPE|DESCRIPTION|
|:-----  |:-----|-----                           |
|error_code |number   |0  |

pages.title: Send animation
pages.content:
Welcome to the Divoom API

    
##### command description

- send animation to device, and device will loop animation。 
This method only accepts one picture of animation at a time, and the picture format must be based on Base64 encoded jpg data.
If the animation is composed of N pictures, it will be sent in N times, one picture data will be sent each time with the picture offset。

##### Request URL
- ` Hardware version 400 is used“ http://IP:80/post " `
- ` Hardware version 402 is used“ http://IP:9000/divoom_api `
  
##### Request method
- POST 

##### para

|Name|DATA TYPE|DESCRIPTION|
|:----    |:----- |-----   |
|Command |string |Draw/SendHttpGif  |
|LocalToken |Number |LocalToken is obtained from the device's settings |
|LcdArray |Array |[1,0,0,0,0] 1:display;0:pass， it must be same in all frames |
|PicNum |number |   the include single pictures of the animation and smaller than 60 |
|PicWidth |number |   the pixels of the animation, and only support the 16,32,64,128  |
|PicOffset |number |  the picture offset start from 0. eg:0,1,2,3,4,PicNum-1  |
|PicID |number |  the animation ID, every animation must have unique ID and auto increase,It's getting bigger and start with 1, example: the current gif id is 100, and then next gif's id should be greater than or equal to 101|
|PicSpeed |number |  the animation speed, it bases on ms |
|PicData |string |  the picutre Base64 encoded JPG data(https://www.rapidtables.com/web/tools/base64-encode.html), The JPEG data is  all binary data of the jpg file |


##### request example 
we will send the gif with two frames, we will send two times,the below are two packets, the  "PicOffset=0" packet should be sended first， and the "PicOffset=1" should be sended later.
``` 
 the first packet:
 {
 "Command":"Draw/SendHttpGif",
 "LocalToken":229930
 "LcdArray":[1,1,0,1,1],
 "PicNum":2,
 "PicWidth":64,
 "PicOffset":0,
 "PicID":3,
 "PicSpeed":100,
 "PicData":""
}

the second packet
{
 "Command":"Draw/SendHttpGif",
 "LocalToken":229930
 "LcdArray":[1,1,0,1,1],
 "PicNum":2,
 "PicWidth":64,
 "PicOffset":1,
 "PicID":3,
 "PicSpeed":100,
 "PicData":""
}
```

  {

  }
```

pages.title: Enter custom display mode
pages.content:
Welcome to the Divoom API

    
##### command description

- Enter custom display mode and accept custom commands for display.
DispList  supports the following display elements:
1: Text：up to six custom text display elements; 
2: Image：Up to ten image display elements; 
3: NetData：Up to six network requests; You can refer to the document“ https://docin.divoom-gz.com/web/#/5/145 ”
4: Time：　Time display ();
5: Date：Date display();
6: Weather: Weather display(Weather Must include a webp animation with 10 images, each representing a different type of weather, in the following order: sunny day，Cloudy day，Rainy day ,snow  day,Frog  day,sunny night ,Cloudy night ,Rainy night ,snow night ,Frog  night ); 
7: Temperature: Temperature display(Temperature);
8: MonYear: MonYear(2025-08);
9: Mday: Mday(the month day);
10:Year; 
11:Month;
12:Week;

##### Request URL
- ` http://IP:9000/divoom_api `
  
##### Request method
- GET

|->FontColor |string | #FFFFFF.     |

|->RuleInfo |string | This is the data parsing rule for network requests, which can be referred to“ https://docin.divoom-gz.com/web/#/5/145 ”.     |

pages.title: command url
pages.content:
Welcome to the Divoom API

##### Command description

Control AstroToo and manage local photos and clock faces from a client on the same LAN. This reference covers device status, system settings, photo management, local clock editing, and tools.

##### Request URL

`http://IP:9000/divoom_api`

Replace `IP` with the device IPv4 address from your router or DHCP client list. The client must be able to reach the device on port 9000.

##### Request method

POST

`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`

Place Command and all business parameters in the JSON body. Command names and parameter spelling are case-sensitive. The current LAN service requires no device API key, account login, or token. Use it on a trusted LAN. ShowDoc publishing credentials are unrelated to device requests.

##### Request example

```json
{"Command":"Device/GetHardwareVersion"}
```

```bash
curl --max-time 15 -X POST 'http://192.168.1.50:9000/divoom_api' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
  --data-raw '{"Command":"Sys/GetBrightness"}'
```

##### Response example

```json
{"Command":"Sys/GetBrightness","ReturnCode":0,"Brightness":50}
```

##### Return value

| Name | Data type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ReturnCode | integer | 0 means firmware reported success. A nonzero value is a failure. |
| ReturnMessage | string | Optional result or error text. |
| Command | string | Response command when included. |
| Other fields | varies | Business data is returned at the root of the JSON object. |

HTTP 200 alone is not success. Reject invalid JSON, missing ReturnCode, or nonzero ReturnCode. An acknowledgement can precede visible or background work; read back the state. Do not automatically retry a write after a timeout.

##### Request limits

- JSON requests and responses have a 65536-byte limit. Serialize requests per device and use smaller list pages if needed.
- Use a 15-second timeout for ordinary JSON requests. Media uploads can take longer; choose a timeout appropriate to the file and network.
- Use numeric 0 and 1 for switches unless a page explicitly specifies JSON booleans.
- Firmware may include DeviceId, PacketFlag, or DeviceType. PacketFlag is not a reliable request correlation value. Do not require those optional fields in every result; identify the model using Device/GetHardwareVersion.
- Local commands can update device state while normal firmware background reporting continues. Local access is not a promise that the entire device makes no outbound network requests.

##### File transfer

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| POST /upload | Photo-library media upload with Photo/LocalAddToAlbum metadata. |
| POST /upload_local_asset | Stage one image for a local clock element or preview. |
| POST /create_local_clock | Create a local clock with one background image. |
| POST /patch_local_clock | Patch a local clock with one background image. |
| POST /replace_clock_dial_bg | Replace one clock background. |
| GET or HEAD /userdata/... | Read a media, thumbnail, or screenshot path returned by the device. |

Clock multipart requests require JSON first and one file second. Each part must have Content-Length. The following standard-library Python helper builds that body. It is suitable for clock images; do not buffer a large video in memory using this example.

```python
import json
import mimetypes
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
from uuid import uuid4

def upload_clock_image(ip, route, metadata, image_path):
    image = Path(image_path)
    payload = image.read_bytes()
    metadata_bytes = json.dumps(metadata).encode("utf-8")
    boundary = "AstroToo" + uuid4().hex
    mime = mimetypes.guess_type(image.name)[0] or "application/octet-stream"
    first = ("--" + boundary + "\r\n"
             'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="json"\r\n'
             "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8\r\n"
             "Content-Length: " + str(len(metadata_bytes)) + "\r\n\r\n").encode("ascii")
    second = ("\r\n--" + boundary + "\r\n"
              'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="asset.bin"\r\n'
              "Content-Type: " + mime + "\r\n"
              "Content-Length: " + str(len(payload)) + "\r\n\r\n").encode("ascii")
    body = first + metadata_bytes + second + payload + ("\r\n--" + boundary + "--\r\n").encode("ascii")
    request = Request("http://" + ip + ":9000" + route, data=body, method="POST",
                      headers={"Content-Type": "multipart/form-data; boundary=" + boundary})
    with urlopen(request, timeout=60) as response:
        result = json.load(response)
    if result.get("ReturnCode") != 0:
        raise RuntimeError(result.get("ReturnMessage", "Upload failed"))
    return result

print(upload_clock_image("192.168.1.50", "/upload_local_asset",
                         {"Command": "Device/UploadLocalAsset"}, "element.png"))
```

##### Compatibility

Reference source: production hardware 530, source firmware version 530056. This is the source baseline, not a minimum-version or device-test certification. Read hardware and capabilities on the target device before integration. Physical-device smoke-test results for firmware 530056 are recorded in the verification section below; they do not establish compatibility with every firmware or parameter combination.

This edition excludes cloud accounts, marketplace, sharing, restore from server, OTA, storage formatting, and commands with incomplete or misleading behavior. A standalone clock-selection/list interface is not included in this edition. Create or patch a local clock, then confirm the displayed ClockId.

##### Physical device verification on 2026-10-20

**Result: SUMMARY.** All 47 command or multipart entries from the original published list were exercised, together with GET and HEAD media download. Read the per-page results: an HTTP 200 or ReturnCode 0 was not counted as proof of visible behavior. This was a functional smoke test of hardware 530 / firmware 530056, not an endurance, power-loss, reboot, or full boundary test.

Tested on AstroToo Hardware 530 / firmware 530056. This result is specific to that firmware and the stated test case.

pages.title: Upload local photo or video
pages.content:
Welcome to the Divoom API

##### Command description

Upload media bytes to the device and queue the media for insertion into an existing local album.

##### Request URL

`http://IP:9000/upload`

##### Request method

POST

`Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=BOUNDARY`

##### Parameters

| Name | Data type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command | string | Required. `Photo/LocalAddToAlbum`. |
| ClockId | integer | Required. Existing normal local album ID >= 100000. |
| ParentItemId, ParentClockId | integer | Required. Use 0 for standalone local albums. |
| UserId | integer | Required. Local owner metadata; use 0 when no application user is associated. |
| PhotoX, PhotoY | integer | Required. Crop or positioning metadata; use 0 for an uncropped image. |
| PhotoWidth, PhotoHeight | integer | Required. Actual media dimensions in pixels. |
| PhotoIndex | integer | Required. Zero-based index in this transfer batch. |
| PhotoTotalCnt | integer | Required. Number of media items in the batch; 1 for one item. |
| PhotoFlag | integer | Required. Batch marker; keep it consistent within a batch and use a different value for a new batch. |
| SendTime | number | Required. Saved time in Unix milliseconds; local database storage uses milliseconds. |
| TakingTime | number | Required. Capture time in Unix milliseconds; firmware converts this field to seconds. |
| FileName | string | Required. Bare media filename matching the multipart filename, below 128 UTF-8 bytes. |
| PreviewFileName | string | Required. Empty string for an image; bare uploaded preview filename for a video, below 128 UTF-8 bytes. |
| PhotoTitle | string | Required. UTF-8 title, below 512 bytes; an empty title is allowed. |

##### Request example

```json
{
  "Command": "Photo/LocalAddToAlbum",
  "ClockId": 110001,
  "ParentItemId": 0,
  "ParentClockId": 0,
  "UserId": 0,
  "PhotoX": 0,
  "PhotoY": 0,
  "PhotoWidth": 480,
  "PhotoHeight": 480,
  "PhotoIndex": 0,
  "PhotoTotalCnt": 1,
  "PhotoFlag": 1792368000,
  "SendTime": 1792368000000,
  "TakingTime": 1792368000000,
  "FileName": "desk.jpg",
  "PreviewFileName": "",
  "PhotoTitle": "Desk photo"
}
```

Send the metadata above as the first JSON part and the media as the next file part. For a video, include its WebP preview as a further file part and set PreviewFileName accordingly. Every file part must include its own Content-Length. Use matching, unique bare filenames; do not reuse the name of another staged upload.

Example structure, with placeholder lengths replaced by actual UTF-8 and file byte counts:

```text
--BOUNDARY
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="json"
Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8
Content-Length: <JSON_BYTES>

<Photo/LocalAddToAlbum JSON>
--BOUNDARY
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="desk.jpg"
Content-Type: image/jpeg
Content-Length: <FILE_BYTES>

<binary file bytes>
--BOUNDARY--
```

All multipart lines use CRLF. For this legacy media route, send the complete JSON part and its following boundary in the first HTTP body data block; the parser does not assemble fragmented metadata headers. Validate your HTTP client's upload behavior before deployment.

##### Response example

```json
{
  "ReturnCode": 0
}
```

Example values are illustrative. Additional response fields may be present.

##### Return value

| Name | Data type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ReturnCode | integer | 0: firmware reported success; nonzero: failure. |
| ReturnMessage | string | Optional result or error text. |

##### Notes

The complete HTTP body must not exceed 536870912 bytes, including all parts. The capability response declares videos up to 1800 seconds; enforce this client-side. Use media decodable by the target firmware. MP4 video playback depends on its codec/profile and resolution; a container extension alone does not guarantee compatibility. Upload images first when integrating. ReturnCode 0 acknowledges transport handling, not successful decode or database insertion. Query Photo/GetPhotoList to confirm the new media. Do not send a second LocalAddToAlbum command after this upload: the upload handler already queues it. The staged files are moved into the library in the background. Use a local album returned by `Photo/GetLocalAlbumList`. The local album ID is named `ClockId`; local photo-library album IDs are at least 100000. Use the [AstroToo watchface visual editor](https://github.com/DivoomDevelop/divoom-watchface-visual-editor_AstroToo) to design and preview a 480 by 480 clock, choose templates, and edit layout, fonts, colors and images. Use [mcp-divoom-lan](https://github.com/DivoomDevelop/mcp-divoom-lan) when an MCP-capable AI client should inspect or edit a device. Follow that repository's build/client setup. Read device identity, capabilities, the existing local clock and available fonts before writes. MCP-managed create/patch calls can use an internal managed slot: follow the wrapper's current parameter contract rather than assuming raw HTTP ClockId allocation rules apply.

##### Local workflow

1. Confirm Hardware 530 and the 480 by 480 canvas.
2. Read the clock and choose a font with AvailableLocally true.
3. Build or preview the design with AstroToo templates and element catalogs.
4. Upload each element asset sequentially through /upload_local_asset and bind its temporary local:// reference. Submit one JPEG or WebP background of exactly 480 by 480 pixels and less than 512000 bytes with create/patch.
5. Read the saved clock and obtain a fresh screenshot to verify the result.

The linked projects offer features beyond this local API reference. Use their local editing features; cloud publishing, review, restore, discovery services and market data are outside this tested scope. A tool exposing a command does not establish that command works on a particular firmware. This reference still excludes standalone clock selection and cloud-related operations. Do not use the acknowledged-but-ineffective UTC-setting or photo-player transition calls as successful workflows.

pages.content:
# We will introduce DataParsingRules and InputUrlAddress in DIY Net Data Clock。

## 1： InputUrlAddress will be the URL address of the data request.The data format is JSON format.
eg: InputUrlAddress is "http://app.divoom-gz.com/User/GetUserData?DeviceId=300043458".
The data returned by the URL request is as follows：
{
    "ReturnCode": 0,
    "ReturnMessage": "",
    "Nickname": "Divoom-Developer",
    "HeadId": "group1/M00/12/9E/eEwpPWLpNhWEI97CAAAAAPpA5X01371922",
    "Level": 20,
    "Score": 1862,
    "LikeCnt": 0,
    "FansCnt": 44,
    "DeviceId": 300043458
}
## 2：DataParsingRules are rules for extracting display data from URL returned data。
DataParsingRules will be a string：
eg:object1,object1-2,object1-3,n:dispNumber;
object1,object1-2,object1-3,s:dispString;
object1,object1-2,object1-3,object4,n:dispNumber;
n:dispNumber;
s:dispString;

Different objects are separated by ',', and the last level of data is represented by 'n' for numbers and's' for strings. The rule is case sensitive.

### 1):the Rule of the divoom respone data:
{
    "ReturnCode": 0,
    "ReturnMessage": "",
    "Nickname": "DivoomTest",
    "HeadId": "group1/M00/05/2A/L1ghbmGdopOEP45jAAAAAIB05eo4227145",
    "DispData": {
        "LikeCnt": 519947,
        "FansCnt": 14654,
        "UserInfo": {
            "Level": 21,
            "Score": 603141
        }
    }
}
The DataParsingRules of  “Nickname” is “s:Nickname”
The DataParsingRules of  “LikeCnt” is “dispData,n:LikeCnt”
The DataParsingRules of  “FansCnt” is “dispData,n:FansCnt”
The DataParsingRules of  “Level” is “dispData,UserInfo,n:Level”
